P1.evidence: Setter mentioned without a read-back: 'I know you spoke with Kim. He gave me like a little bit of an overview.' Same three-part frame as every call in this batch — 'I just want to get a good idea where you're at, build out what it is that you want. And then if it's a good fit, we can talk about the coaching' — with no 'what's in the way' and no 'what you need'. Agreement asked as 'Alrighty?' and received ('Mhm. Cool.'). Open question ran verbatim.

P2.evidence: Injuries were handled properly and are the one bright spot: he pursued a vague phrase into a specific complaint ('when you say your body's screaming at you, like what's actually going on there?'), screened it clinically ('do you get any pain that goes down your leg?'), and dated it ('how long has that been a thing for'). Everything else is absent. No age, height or weight at any point. Occupation volunteered, not asked. No health conditions, no diet, no sleep, no energy, no results question. Training was probed for content ('what's kind of been your bread and butter, I guess, with training recently?') but never for frequency.

P3.evidence: Strong on the vertical ladder, absent on the horizontal one. Six-month framing ran ('where would you want to be six months down the line?'), and he pushed twice past the first answer — 'What would even change? So let's say you'll move more freely or more spry, like what changes?' and 'what would it be like to not have to be crippled then?'. The reflect-back was the best in the batch and was checked rather than asserted: 'this is what it sounds like to me, and tell me if this is wrong... you know you should do it, but you don't really want to' — confirmed by the prospect. Never asked who else this impacts, which for a man in the second year of his own construction business with a back that stops him standing up is the obvious commercial and personal lever. The identity work ('picture the most whole version of you') arrived after the no, as parting advice rather than as goal development.

P4.evidence: The phase ran essentially as written and is the strongest execution of any phase in this batch. Past attempts surfaced (calisthenics, push-ups, pull-ups, morning stretching routines), outcome named by the prospect ('nothing seems to stick'), and the why asked directly — 'Why do you think that is?' — producing all-in-then-fade-out and post-work exhaustion. The blocker question was then asked again later and better: 'What do you feel like that resistance is?', which produced the real gap in the prospect's own words — stubborn self-reliance, living in his head, and overwhelm at not knowing what to do. The scripted 'why can't you stick to it on your own' ran as a variant rather than as the question: 'the truth is you can do it on your own, everyone can... but it's harder.'

P5.evidence: 'What happens if you don't?' ran the intent of the two-year question without the horizon, and the answer ('hopefully I find the motivation to nip this in the butt') was not pressed. Neither the settle-for question nor 'why not' was asked. The line in the sand ran repeatedly and in the script's own language — 'people who are super committed and ready to draw a line in the sand and change' — supported by the Ferrari and horse-to-water metaphors.

P6.evidence: P6c is textbook and is the reason this call scores respectably despite losing: the rep asked the readiness question three separate times, returned to consequence and resistance each time hesitation appeared, and explicitly refused to move forward without a yes — 'I want to make sure it's something you want to do before I even tell you about it.' He got the no and stopped. The belief question was asserted rather than asked ('You have the potential to achieve anything that you want... the truth is you can do it'), and the all-in question was never put.

P11.evidence: No close attempted and no offer presented. Price appeared only as an illustration inside the rep's argument for why the prospect should not buy yet, so no payment or onboarding step was reachable.

objection_plays.detail: Fear and resistance were the whole call. The rep diagnosed rather than rebutted, which was appropriate, and did run one scripted asset — the plane bridge, as 'it's like jumping out the plane when you go skydiving, you know, it's the hard part'. He also improvised well with the 10pm-dishes image, which the prospect adopted and extended. Not run: the certainty question, the pleasure-versus-pain framing, and the burned-before analogy. He never asked 'how will you know if you never actually try?', which was directly available.

Trigger was the second-year business and post-work exhaustion. The rep ran a solid make-time-not-find-time reframe — 'The truth is, you can't find the time. It's just, it's more making it' — but none of the scripted OD moves: no 'things never slow down', no 'the longer you wait the harder this gets', which was unusually well-supported here by a back complaint already a year old, and no 'what if all you had to do was show up and everything else was handled', which is the exact answer to 'when I try to work out, it's overwhelming'.

'Maybe I'll come back to this' is the trigger, and no OA move ran. This was a deliberate choice rather than a lapse — the rep had already accepted a clear no and switched to advice — but it should be recorded as a miss for the rollup: no 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you there', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no 'that man you want to be, how does HE decide right now?', which was in fact the exact frame he then used as unpaid parting advice.

Script gap: there is no protocol for a principled disqualification. The rep decided early that the prospect was not committed, spent eighteen minutes testing that rather than selling, then declined to present the offer at all. The playbook has no path for this — no criteria for when to disqualify, no defined outcome, no nurture or re-engagement mechanism, and no way to distinguish it in reporting from a lost deal. He improvised it well, but the business currently has no way to tell a disciplined disqualification from a failed call.

Clinical-fit trigger with no scripted play, in the mildest form seen in this batch. A year of intermittent lower-back pain severe enough that the prospect sometimes cannot stand up directly. The rep screened for radiating leg pain — genuinely good, and unique in this batch — but the playbook gave him nothing to do with a negative answer, and he moved to exercise advice rather than to any question about clinical assessment.

notes: Loses the deal and scores well, which is the point of independent scoring: the commitment gate ran properly, past attempts and root cause were the best in the batch, and the rep refused to sell into a no. Two coachable gaps remain — no baseline at all (no age, weight, sleep, diet or energy on a 26-minute call), and no 'who else does this impact' on a prospect whose back pain is actively degrading a business he owns.
